traits.forehead: Prominently convex, ultra-domed forehead acting as a physical shield protecting the eyes from harsh desert sun.
traits.ears: Extremely long, pendulous, drooping ears folded like a curling leaf with a characteristic notch near the tip.
traits.horns: Curved backwards and downwards, then sweeping upwards and outwards in a half-moon curl.
traits.hump_dewlap: Pronounced thoracic hump and voluminous, loose pendulous dewlap.
traits.coat: Mottled rich red, white patches, reddish-brown, or speckled 'speckled red' coat.

distinguishing_vs.difference: Gir has an ultra-domed bulging forehead and long pendulous leaf-like curled ears; Sahiwal has a flat skull, shorter ears, and a deeper loose naval flap ('Lola').
Red Sindhi is uniformly deep red and more compact with standard ears; Gir has folded pendulous ears and unmistakable cranial convexity.

traits.forehead: Broad, level forehead with a slight groove between the horn roots.
traits.ears: Small, pointed, erect ears carried horizontally and alert.
traits.horns: Strong, stout horns curving backwards, outwards, and inward at tips, spaced widely at the base.
traits.hump_dewlap: Well-developed, compact firm hump in bulls; moderate thin dewlap with delicate folds.
traits.coat: Bulls are grey with dark grey/black shading on hump, poll, knees, and quarters; cows are brilliant white or light grey.

distinguishing_vs.difference: Kangayam has shorter, stouter horns curving outward and backward; Hallikar has very long, sharp, backward-swept horns emerging close together from a narrow poll.
Umblachery has distinct white star marking on forehead and white socks on all four legs, whereas Kangayam has solid grey shading.

traits.forehead: Broad, elliptical skull between horn bases with prominent stumpy eyes and black rimmed sockets.
traits.ears: Moderately long, drooping slightly, alert and cleanly tapered.
traits.horns: Short, stumpy horns growing outwards and backwards.
traits.hump_dewlap: Massive, erect, muscular thoracic hump in bulls; heavy, pendulous dewlap extending in deep folds to the chest.
traits.coat: Glossy porcelain white or light grey with dark markings around eyes, hooves, and switch of tail.

distinguishing_vs.difference: Ongole is much larger and more muscular with a massive thoracic hump and heavy folded dewlap; Hariana has a flatter skull, smaller hump, and compact frame.
Krishna Valley has a distinct bulging forehead with curved horns and shorter body; Ongole is long-bodied with clean stumpy horns and majestic stance.

traits.forehead: Medium broad, flat or slightly depressed forehead without cranial doming.
traits.ears: Medium sized, drooping downwards with black fringed edges.
traits.horns: Short, thick, stumpy horns rarely exceeding 10-12 cm.
traits.hump_dewlap: Loose, heavy, voluminous dewlap and pendulous sheath ('Lola'); large fleshy hump in males.
traits.coat: Reddish-brown, pale red, or brownish-dun, often with white flashes along the underline.

distinguishing_vs.difference: Sahiwal is larger, heavier, paler red/dun with much looser pendulous skin and navel flap; Red Sindhi is compact with deeper mahogany-red color and tighter sheath.
Sahiwal lacks the convex domed forehead and long leaf-curled ears of the Gir.

traits.forehead: Narrow, prominent forehead with a distinct vertical groove in the center.
traits.horns: Long, sharp, elegant horns emerging close together from the poll, sweeping backwards and upwards in a graceful curve with sharp tapering tips.
traits.hump_dewlap: High, firm, forward-inclined hump; thin, moderately deep dewlap.
traits.coat: Dark grey to light grey with white patches on face and muzzle; bulls develop deep blackish-grey shoulders.

distinguishing_vs.difference: Hallikar horns emerge close together and curve backwards in an even arch; Amritmahal horns sweep backwards and outwards before curving sharply inward at the tips.
Hallikar has a longer face and darker facial markings; Khillari is pale pinkish-white with backward horns pointing almost straight back.

traits.forehead: Broad forehead with flat profile between diminutive horn buds.
traits.horns: Short, crescent-shaped horns curving backwards and outwards (often 5-8 cm).
traits.hump_dewlap: Small, compact hump; short delicate dewlap.
traits.coat: White, light brown, grey, or dark brown; short legs with height rarely exceeding 70-90 cm.
traits.build: Compact, diminutive, low-set stature with exceptionally sweet countenance.

Malnad Gidda is typically black or dark brown with rainforest adaptation; Punganur is creamy-white or fawn with low-slung body.

traits.forehead: Broad, dished or slightly concave forehead between the massive horn roots.
traits.ears: Very large, open, pendulous ears drooping outward like open lily petals.
traits.horns: Magnificent lyre-shaped horns: thick at base, growing vertically, curving outwards and inwards at the sharp tips.
